title: Numbers & Colors
description: Master counting from 0 to 100, learn all colors, describe quantities, sizes, and use numbers in everyday situations like prices, ages, and phone numbers.

grammar.title: Numbers 0–30 — The Building Blocks
grammar.content:
Learn to count from zero to thirty. These are the foundation for all larger numbers.

0 = cero
1 = uno (un before masculine nouns: un libro)
2 = dos
3 = tres
4 = cuatro
5 = cinco
6 = seis
7 = siete
8 = ocho
9 = nueve
10 = diez
11 = once
12 = doce
13 = trece
14 = catorce
15 = quince
16 = dieciséis
17 = diecisiete
18 = dieciocho
19 = diecinueve
20 = veinte
21 = veintiuno (veintiún before masculine nouns)
22 = veintidós
23 = veintitrés
24 = veinticuatro
25 = veinticinco
26 = veintiséis
27 = veintisiete
28 = veintiocho
29 = veintinueve
30 = treinta

KEY RULE: uno → un before masculine singular nouns
- un libro (a book) ✓
- una casa (a house) ✓

KEY RULE: veintiuno → veintiún before masculine singular nouns
- veintiún dólares (21 dollars) ✓
- veintiuna personas (21 people — feminine) ✓
examples:
Tengo tres gatos. (I have three cats.)
Son las cinco. (It's five o'clock.)
Quiero dos cafés. (I want two coffees.)
Tengo dieciséis años. (I'm sixteen years old.)
Cuestan veintiún euros. (They cost 21 euros.)

Uno de mis amigos es doctor. (One of my friends is a doctor.)
Tengo una hermana. (I have one sister.)
Es el número diez. (It's the number ten.)
Vivo en el piso veintitrés. (I live on floor 23.)

grammar.title: Numbers 30–100 — Building Larger Numbers
grammar.content:
For numbers 31–99, use 'y' (and) between tens and units:

30 = treinta
31 = treinta y uno
32 = treinta y dos
...
40 = cuarenta
41 = cuarenta y uno
...
50 = cincuenta
60 = sesenta
70 = setenta
80 = ochenta
90 = noventa
100 = cien

For 101–999, use 'ciento' (NOT 'cien'):
101 = ciento uno
200 = doscientos / doscientas
300 = trescientos / trescientas
500 = quinientos / quinientas
1000 = mil

CRITICAL: 'cien' is ONLY used for exactly 100.
- Cien personas (100 people) ✓
- Ciento uno (101) ✓

Hundred forms (gender agreement):
- doscientos (m) / doscientas (f)
- trescientos (m) / trescientas (f)
- quinientos (m) / quinientas (f)
examples:
Treinta y tres personas. (33 people.)
Cuarenta y dos días. (42 days.)
Ciento diez euros. (110 euros.)
Doscientas casas. (200 houses.)
Quinientos años. (500 years.)
Mil dólares. (1,000 dollars.)

Son las tres y media. (It's 3:30.)
Tiene cuarenta y cinco años. (He/She is 45 years old.)
Hay sesenta minutos en una hora. (There are 60 minutes in an hour.)
Cien personas en la fila. (100 people in line.)

grammar.title: Colors — Agreement with Nouns
grammar.content:
Colors must agree with the noun they describe in gender (and number).

COLORS THAT CHANGE (m → f):
- rojo → roja (red)
- blanco → blanca (white)
- negro → negra (black)
- amarillo → amarilla (yellow)
- morado → morada (purple)
- dorado → dorada (gold)
- plateado → plateada (silver)
- burdeos → (usually invariant in practice)
- crema → (feminine only, for cream)

INVARIABLE COLORS (same for m/f):
- azul (blue)
- verde (green)
- gris (gray)
- naranja (orange)
- rosa (pink)
- beige (beige)
- turquesa (turquoise)
- celeste (light blue)
- marrón (brown)
- café (coffee/brown)

Plural forms:
- el coche rojo → los coches rojos (the red cars)
- la casa blanca → las casas blancas (the white houses)
- el perro azul → los perros azules (the blue dogs)

PATTERN: Add -s (vowel ending) or -es (consonant ending)
examples:
El coche es rojo. (The car is red.)
La casa es blanca. (The house is white.)
El cielo es azul. (The sky is blue.)
La camiseta es verde. (The t-shirt is green.)
Los zapatos son negros. (The shoes are black.)
Las flores son rosas. (The flowers are pink.)

Unas camisas azules. (Some blue shirts.)
Unas camisas rojas. (Some red shirts.)
Unos libros dorados. (Some gold books.)
Una mesa marrón. (A brown table.)
Un gato negro. (A black cat.)

grammar.title: Quantifiers — Mucho, Poco, Bastante
grammar.content:
Quantifiers change form to match the noun in gender and number.

mucho (a lot/much) → mucha → muchos → muchas
poco (a little/few) → poca → pocos → pocas
bastante (quite a lot) → bastante (invariable, but can add -s for plural)

Use 'mucho' with uncountable nouns:
- Tengo mucho tiempo. (I have a lot of time.)
- Hay mucha gente. (There is a lot of people.)

Use 'muchos/muchas' with countable nouns:
- Tengo muchos libros. (I have many books.)
- Hay pocas manzanas. (There are few apples.)

Poco can mean 'a little' (uncountable) or 'few' (countable):
- Tengo poca agua. (I have a little water.)
- Hay pocos coches. (There are few cars.)

bastante works as both singular and plural:
- Tengo bastante dinero. (I have quite a lot of money.)
- Hay bastantes personas. (There are quite a few people.)
examples:
Tengo muchos hermanos. (I have many siblings.)
Hay pocas sillas. (There are few chairs.)
Tengo bastante hambre. (I'm quite hungry.)
¿Cuántas manzanas quieres? — Quiero tres. (How many apples do you want? — I want three.)
No hay mucho tiempo. (There isn't much time.)

grammar.title: Using Numbers — Prices, Ages, Phone Numbers
grammar.content:
Common situations with numbers:

PRICES:
- ¿Cuánto cuesta? (How much does it cost?) — singular
- ¿Cuánto cuestan? (How much do they cost?) — plural
- Cuesta diez euros. (It costs 10 euros.)
- Cuestan veinticinco dólares. (They cost 25 dollars.)
- Son cien euros. (They're 100 euros.)

AGES:
- ¿Cuántos años tienes? (How old are you?)
- Tengo veinticinco años. (I'm 25 years old.)
- Tiene cuarenta años. (He/She is 40 years old.)
- NOTE: No 'tener' agreement with 'años' — always plural

PHONE NUMBERS:
- ¿Cuál es tu número? (What's your number?)
- Mi número es... (My number is...)
- Leo los dígitos uno por uno: seis, siete, ocho... (I read digits one by one: six, seven, eight...)
- Sometimes use 'y' for pairs: seis y siete (67)

ORDINALS (first, second, third) — basic forms:
- primero/a (first)
- segundo/a (second)
- tercer/tercera (third)
- Used for floors, dates, rankings

¿CUÁNTO must agree with the noun:
- ¿Cuántos libros? (masc. plural)
- ¿Cuántas casas? (fem. plural)
- ¿Cuánto dinero? (masc. singular)
- ¿Cuánta agua? (fem. singular)
examples:
¿Cuánto cuesta? — Cuesta cinco euros. (How much does it cost? — It costs 5 euros.)
Tengo treinta y dos años. (I'm 32 years old.)
Tengo dos hermanos y una hermana. (I have two brothers and one sister.)
El libro cuesta doce euros. (The book costs 12 euros.)
Mi teléfono es seis, siete, ocho, nueve. (My phone is 6, 7, 8, 9.)

¿Cuántas manzanas quieres? — Quiero tres manzanas. (How many apples do you want? — I want three apples.)
¿Cuántos libros tienes? — Tengo muchos. (How many books do you have? — I have many.)
Vivo en el tercer piso. (I live on the third floor.)
Ella es la primera de la clase. (She is first in the class.)

grammar.title: Telling Time with Numbers
grammar.content:
Telling time uses numbers extensively.

EXACT HOURS:
- Es la una. (It's 1:00) — singular!
- Son las dos. (It's 2:00) — plural for 2+
- Son las tres. (It's 3:00)
- Son las doce. (It's 12:00)

HALF AND QUARTER:
- y media = and half (:30) — Son las tres y media.
- y cuarto = and quarter (:15) — Son las dos y cuarto.
- menos cuarto = minus quarter (:45) — Son las cinco menos cuarto.

MINUTES:
- y cinco = and five (:05) — Son las cuatro y cinco.
- y diez = and ten (:10) — Son las nueve y diez.
- menos cinco = minus five (:55) — Son las siete menos cinco.

MORNING / AFTERNOON / NIGHT:
- de la mañana (AM) — Son las ocho de la mañana.
- de la tarde (afternoon) — Son las cinco de la tarde.
- de la noche (evening/night) — Son las diez de la noche.

Specific times:
- en punto (sharp) — Son las tres en punto.
- media hora (half an hour) — Faltan media hora.
- una hora (one hour)

24-hour format (common in schedules):
- Treinta y cuatro horas? No! Las diecisiete horas (5 PM).
- Las ocho de la mañana = las 08:00
- Las veinte horas = 8 PM (20:00)
examples:
Son las tres en punto. (It's exactly 3:00.)
Son las dos y media. (It's 2:30.)
Son las cinco y cuarto. (It's 5:15.)
Son las siete menos cuarto. (It's 6:45.)
¿Qué hora es? — Son las diez y diez. (What time is it? — It's 10:10.)

Clase a las ocho de la mañana. (Class at 8 AM.)
La película a las siete y media. (The movie at 7:30.)
Salgo a las tres y veinte. (I leave at 3:20.)
¿A qué hora es la fiesta? — A las nueve. (What time is the party? — At 9.)

pronunciation.title: Numbers — Stress and Accent Marks
pronunciation.content:
Pay attention to stress (accent marks) in Spanish numbers.

ACCENT MARKS on numbers:
- dieciséis (die-see-SEHS) — accent on 'e'
- veintidós (bain-tee-DOHS) — accent on 'o'
- veintitrés (bain-tee-TREHS) — accent on 'e'
- veintiséis (bain-tee-see-SEHS) — accent on 'e'
- cuarenta y dos (kwa-REN-tah ee DOHS)
- cincuenta (seen-KWEHN-tah) — no accent, stress on 'cuen'
- sesenta (seh-SEN-tah) — stress on 'sen'
- setenta (seh-TEN-tah) — stress on 'ten'
- ochenta (oh-CHEN-tah) — stress on 'chen'
- noventa (no-SEN-tah) — stress on 'ven'

GENERAL STRESS RULE:
- Words ending in n, s, or vowel → stress on second-to-last syllable
  Example: veintitRÉs → has accent because stress is on last syllable 'és'
  Example: cincuenta → no accent, stress on 'cuen' (second-to-last)

NUMBERS WITHOUT ACCENT MARKS:
- uno (OO-noh), dos (dohs), tres (trehs), cuatro (KWAH-tro)
- cinco (SEEN-ko), seis (seys), siete (SYEH-teh), ocho (OH-cho)
- diez (dyehs), once (OH-nseh), doce (DOH-seh)
- treinta (treh-YEN-tah), cuarenta (kwa-REN-tah)
- cien (syen), mil (meel)

NOTE: 'veintiuno' drops the 'o' before a masculine noun:
- veintiún dólares (21 dollars)
- veintiuna casas (21 houses)
examples:
dieciséis = die-see-SEHS (16)
veintidós = bain-tee-DOHS (22)
veintitrés = bain-tee-TREHS (23)
veinticuatro = bain-tee-KWAH-tro (24)
cincuenta = seen-KWEHN-tah (50)
sesenta = seh-SEN-tah (60)
setenta = seh-TEN-tah (70)
ochenta = oh-CHEN-tah (80)
noventa = no-SEN-tah (90)
cien = syen (100)

pronunciation.title: Color Names — Pronunciation Guide
pronunciation.content:
Common color pronunciations with key sound patterns.

KEY SPANISH SOUNDS:
- 'j' = strong 'h' sound (like in 'hah')
- 'll' = 'y' sound (like in 'yes')
- 'ñ' = 'ny' sound (like in 'canyon')
- 'v' = sounds like 'b' (soft b)
- 'z' (Spain) = 'th' sound; (Latin America) = 's' sound

COLOR PRONUNCIATIONS:
- rojo = ROH-hoh (j = h sound)
- rojo/a = ROH-hoh / ROH-hah
- azul = ah-SOOL (z = s in Latin America)
- verde = BER-deh (v = b sound)
- amarillo = ah-mah-REE-yoh
- blanco/a = BLAN-ko / BLAN-kah
- negro/a = NEG-roh / NEG-roh-ah
- gris = GRIS (short, crisp)
- naranja = nah-RAN-hah (g = h sound before 'a')
- rosa = ROH-sah
- morado/a = moh-RAH-doh / moh-RAH-dah
- marrón = mah-RON (accent on 'o')
- beige = beh-GEH
- dorado/a = doh-RAH-doh / doh-RAH-dah
- plateado/a = plah-tah-DEH-doh / plah-tah-DEH-dah
- turquesa = door-KES-ah
- celeste = seh-LES-teh
examples:
rojo = ROH-hoh
azul = ah-SOOL
verde = BER-deh
amarillo = ah-mah-REE-yoh
blanco = BLAN-ko
negro = NEG-roh
gris = GRIS
naranja = nah-RAN-hah
rosa = ROH-sah
morado = moh-RAH-doh
marrón = mah-RON
dorado = doh-RAH-doh
plateado = plah-tah-DEH-doh

pronunciation.title: Syllable Division in Numbers
pronunciation.content:
Spanish syllables are divided clearly — each vowel forms its own syllable.

SINGLE-SYLLABLE NUMBERS:
cero (1), dos (1), tres (1), cuatro (2: cua-tro), cinco (2: cin-co)
seis (1), diez (1), once (1), doce (1), cien (1), mil (1)

TWO-SYLLABLE NUMBERS:
uno (u-no), dos (1), tres (1), quatro (cua-tro), cinco (cin-co)
veinte (bain-TEH-teh), treinta (treh-YEN-tah), cuarenta (kwa-REN-tah)
cincuenta (seen-KWEHN-tah), sesenta (seh-SEN-ta), setenta (seh-TEN-tah)
ochenta (oh-CHEN-ta), noventa (no-SEN-ta)

LONGER NUMBERS:
dieciséis (die-see-SEHS) — 3 syllables
veintidós (bain-tee-DOHS) — 3 syllables
veintitrés (bain-tee-TREHS) — 3 syllables
dieciséis (die-see-SEHS) — 3 syllables
cuarenta y uno (kwa-REN-tah ee MOO-noh) — 5 syllables

TIPS FOR PRONUNCIATION:
- Spanish vowels are always short and clear: a, e, i, o, u
- Never glide between vowels
- 'y' between numbers = 'ee' sound
- The accent mark ALWAYS indicates the stressed syllable

PRACTICE PHRASES:
- Tres y medio = tres ee MEH-dio (3.5)
- Cuarenta y cinco = kwa-REN-tah ee SEEN-kwah (45)
- Sesenta y siete = seh-SEN-tah ee SYEH-teh (67)
examples:
Uno: u-no (2 syllables)
Cuatro: cua-tro (2 syllables)
Veinte: bain-TEH-teh (2 syllables)
Treinta: treh-YEN-tah (3 syllables)
Cincuenta: seen-KWEHN-tah (3 syllables)
Dieciséis: die-see-SEHS (3 syllables)
Cuarenta y cinco: kwa-REN-tah ee seen-KWAH (5 syllables)

exercises.question: What is '23' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Veintitrés' = 23. Note the accent mark on the 'e'.

exercises.question: How do you say 'blue' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Azul' = blue. 'Verde' = green. 'Rojo' = red. 'Negro' = black.

exercises.question: What does 'cien' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Cien' = 100. 'Mil' = 1,000. 'Diez' = 10. 'Cincuenta' = 50.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Tengo ___ años.' (I'm 25 years old.)
exercises.explanation: 'Tengo veinticinco años' = I'm 25 years old.

exercises.question: Complete: 'El coche es ___. (The car is red.)'
exercises.explanation: 'Rojo' = red (masculine). 'Roja' would be feminine: 'la casa roja'.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ y uno.' (Thirty-one.)
exercises.explanation: 'Treinta y uno' = 31. Use 'y' (and) between tens and units.

exercises.question: Which color is invariable (same for masculine and feminine)?
exercises.explanation: 'Azul' is invariable — same form for masculine and feminine. The others change: rojo/roja, blanco/blanca, negro/negra.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Cuesta ___ euros.' (It costs 15 euros.)
exercises.explanation: 'Cuesta quince euros' = It costs 15 euros.

exercises.question: What is '100' in Spanish when followed by another number?
exercises.explanation: Use 'ciento' (not 'cien') when followed by another number: 'ciento uno' = 101. Use 'cien' only for exactly 100.

exercises.question: Complete: 'La casa es ___. (The house is white.)'
exercises.explanation: 'Blanca' = white (feminine). 'Blanco' would be masculine: 'el coche blanco'.

exercises.question: How do you say 'sixty-seven' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Sesenta y siete' = 67. Use 'y' between the tens and units.

exercises.question: Which form is correct before a masculine noun?
exercises.explanation: 'Veintiún' (without the 'o') goes before masculine nouns: veintiún dólares.

exercises.question: What is the feminine plural of 'rojo'?
exercises.explanation: 'Rojas' is the feminine plural: las casas rojas. Add -s for vowel endings.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Tengo ___ gatos.' (I have many cats.)
exercises.explanation: 'Muchos' = many (masculine plural). 'Tengo muchos gatos' = I have many cats.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Son las ___ y media.' (It's 3:30.)
exercises.explanation: 'Son las tres y media' = It's 3:30. Note: 'es la una' (1:00) but 'son las...' for 2+.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'The shirt is green.'
exercises.explanation: 'La camisa es verde' = The shirt is green. 'Verde' is invariable (same for masculine and feminine).

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'They cost 42 euros.'
exercises.explanation: 'Cuestan cuarenta y dos euros' = They cost 42 euros. Use 'cuestan' (plural) because 'they' is plural.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'I have two sisters and three brothers.'
exercises.correct: Tengo dos hermanas y tres hermanos
alternatives: Tengo dos hermanas y tres hermanos.
exercises.explanation: 'Tengo dos hermanas y tres hermanos' = I have two sisters and three brothers. Note: hermana (f), hermano (m).

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'The walls are white.'
exercises.explanation: 'Las paredes son blancas' = The walls are white. 'Blancas' is feminine plural to match 'las paredes'.

exercises.question: What time is 'las ocho y media'?
exercises.explanation: 'Las ocho y media' = 8:30. 'Y media' means 'and half' (:30).

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'four hundred'? (masc.)
exercises.explanation: 'Cuatrocientos' = 400 (masculine). 'Cuatrocientas' would be feminine. The 'ciento' form drops to '-cientos/-cientas'.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ son las diez.' (It's 10 o'clock.)
exercises.explanation: 'Son las diez' = It's 10 o'clock. Use 'son las' for all hours except 1:00 (es la una).

exercises.question: Complete: 'Un ___ libro.' (A red book.)
exercises.explanation: 'Un rojo libro' — wait! The adjective typically goes AFTER the noun in Spanish: 'Un libro rojo'. But both positions are grammatically acceptable for color adjectives.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'How much does it cost?'
exercises.explanation: '¿Cuánto cuesta?' = How much does it cost? (singular). For plural items: '¿Cuánto cuestan?'

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'The car is blue and the house is white.'
exercises.correct: El coche es azul y la casa es blanca
alternatives: El coche es azul y la casa es blanca.
exercises.explanation: 'El coche es azul y la casa es blanca.' 'Azul' is invariable. 'Blanca' matches the feminine 'casa'.

exercises.question: What is '0' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Cero' = zero. It's always spelled the same way, no gender variation.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Tengo ___ agua.' (I have a little water.)
exercises.explanation: 'Tengo poca agua' = I have a little water. 'Poca' is feminine singular to match 'agua' (feminine).

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'What time is it?'
exercises.explanation: '¿Qué hora es?' = What time is it? The standard way to ask the time.

exercises.question: Which number is 'mil'?
exercises.explanation: 'Mil' = 1,000. 'Cien' = 100. 'Diez' = 10. 'Mil' has no plural form in standard usage.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Las flores son ___. (The flowers are red.)'
exercises.explanation: 'Rojas' = red (feminine plural). 'Las flores' is feminine plural, so the color must agree.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'It's a quarter past two.'
alternatives: Es un cuarto después de las dos.
exercises.explanation: 'Son las dos y cuarto' = It's a quarter past two (2:15). 'Y cuarto' = and a quarter.

exercises.question: How do you say 'twenty-one' before a masculine noun?
exercises.explanation: 'Veintiún' (without final 'o') is used before masculine nouns: veintiún años, veintiún euros.
